acceptance.evidence: test/index.test.js "AC-1: seeds Work and Home, dedupes names, rejects an empty one, and tags the seeded items" checks the exact rows, the UNIQUE and CHECK rejections, that category_id is nullable, the items_category_id index and the seeded tagging, all against migrations/0003_item_categories.sql.

test/index.test.js "AC-2: an insert naming only title still works; an unknown category_id is rejected" inserts with only a title and gets a null category_id, and expects a FOREIGN KEY error for category_id 999.

test/index.test.js "AC-3: / lists every item in id order..." checks the id order with an uncategorised item added, the exact span markup for a categorised item and the bare <li> for an item with no category.

test/index.test.js "AC-4: / shows All first, then every category by name case-insensitively, with All current" adds the empty lower-case category 'errands', checks the exact ordered link list with its hrefs, and checks that only All is current. URL encoding is also covered by AC-7.
test/index.test.js has two AC-5 tests: Work's items only, in id order, with an unfiled item excluded and only Work current; and a byte-equal page for /?category=Work&x=1 and for /?x=1 against /.
test/index.test.js "AC-6: a category with no items says so, with the filter links" checks 200, the message, no <li>, and that Garden is the only current link.

test/index.test.js "AC-7: a name that needs encoding and escaping..." checks there is no raw <x>, the escaped span and link text, and the href /?category=R%26D%20%3Cx%3E. Requesting that link returns 200 with only Prototype listed.

test/index.test.js it.each "AC-8: %s is a broken link" covers all five paths and checks the 404, the message, the Go back anchor with href="/", the referrer/origin/history.back script, and no <li> or <nav>.
test/index.test.js "AC-9: HEAD answers like GET" expects 200 for / and /?category=Work and 404 for /?category=Wrok.

Verified by review, but the review step was not performed: no browser is available here. I could only read the script in src/index.js (brokenLinkPage). The step also cannot be followed as written. Nothing in the app links to /?category=Wrok, so the reviewer must type it into the address bar. A typed URL sends no referrer, so the first half lands on / and not /?category=Home. The code also adds a `history.length > 1` condition that the spec doesn't describe.

traffic/routes.json lists /?category=Work. tests/traffic-config.test.sh accepts a query route and rejects routes with whitespace, with # or without a leading /. test/traffic.test.js has the AC-11 test for the listed route and checks that seen paths equal [/healthz, ...ROUTES] with the query kept. test/index.test.js "AC-11: the filter route listed for synthetic traffic answers 2xx".

The existing GET / tests (h1, title escaping, 'No items yet.') and the /healthz, 404 and 405 tests are kept unchanged. The only assertion edited is
  • First item
    • , now the AC-3 markup (test/index.test.js:15).

test/apply-migrations.js drops all tables in one batch with defer_foreign_keys. test/index.test.js "AC-13: the test reset copes with the foreign key" expects exactly 4 items after earlier tests inserted rows, which fails if the reset didn't run. Any failure in the reset would also fail every test through beforeEach.

findings.what: AC-10 is verified by review only, and its step cannot be performed as written. The app has no link to /?category=Wrok, so 'navigate to /?category=Wrok' means typing the URL. A typed URL sends no document.referrer, so 'Go back' goes to / rather than /?category=Home. No browser was available to perform the step, so the item is unverified.
findings.fix: Make the step reproducible, for example: open /?category=Home, then in the devtools console run `location.href='/?category=Wrok'` (script navigation sends the same-origin referrer), click Go back and land on /?category=Home. Then have the reviewer perform and record it.

findings.what: The States row '`/`, no items' (filter links shown with All current, Go back hidden) has no test checking those columns. 'says so when the table is empty' only asserts 'No items yet.'. No 200-state test asserts that Go back and the broken-link message are hidden. The `links()` regex only matches `<a href=` and would not see `<a id="back"`.
findings.fix: In the empty-table test, assert currentLinks(html) equals ['All'], that the Work and Home links are present and that there is no <ul>. In the 200-state tests (/, a known category with items, a known category with none), assert the HTML has no 'Go back' and no 'This link seems to be corrupted.'.

findings.what: The Go back script goes back only when `ours && history.length > 1`. The spec decision says it goes back whenever document.referrer is same-origin. The spec names `history.length > 1` only as a rejected design. The extra guard is an undocumented deviation, and the AC-8 test regex doesn't pin the condition.
findings.fix: Either drop `&& history.length > 1` to match the decision, or record in the spec why it is kept (a same-origin page opened in a new tab has nothing to go back to).

findings.what: The spec decision says a later migration that renames or removes `Work` must update traffic/routes.json in the same change, or synthetic traffic fails in production. That constraint appears only in the spec. README.md, CLAUDE.md and the migration don't mention it, so a future agent reading the docs would not know.
findings.fix: Add a line to the CLAUDE.md conventions or the README (or a comment in migrations/0003_item_categories.sql) saying that /?category=Work is in traffic/routes.json and must be updated with any rename or removal of that category.
